messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Silverline commercial request — key routing + residency commit

Laura / Markus / Ben — short ask from the Silverline deal team. Emily (cc'd externally on subsequent emails) sent a requirements packet and they have two gating asks that are determinative for this quarter-close: 

1) A per-customer routing policy so requests from silverline.com always go to a pinned model variant with residency in us-west-2 (customer-controlled CMKs + audit logs).
2) A soft SLA commitment around tail latency for burst windows (they expect < 300ms p50 for embeddings and < 800ms p95 for short chat prompts at peak).

Their legal/procurement team wants these reflected in the quote/commit language before signature. From a sales perspective this deal converts an existing POC to a multi-year reserved contract (~$1.1M ARR). We need a cross-functional decision today on whether Product/Eng can (a) scope an MVP we can commit to in 8 weeks, and (b) provide language the sales team can include in the commercial term sheet.

I've attached their requirements (SIL-Requirements-20280628.pdf) and a very small traffic model they shared. Ben — can you confirm the commercial cadence if we can provide a scoped commitment? Laura / Markus — high level questions: 
- Can we implement a configurable routing policy (tenant pin + region constraint) without a major runtime refactor?
- What minimal telemetry/audit surface do we need to satisfy their compliance ask?

If we can't fully meet both asks, what tradeoffs could we offer as a fall-back (example: regional residency + post-hoc snapshot exports for audits, or a higher-latency SLA with credits)? I want to prepare two options to present to Silverline by EOD.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel | Account Exec, Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — quick assessment from Product.

Short answer: we can deliver a scoped, documented MVP for tenant-level routing + region pinning within 6–10 weeks if we accept the following constraints:

- Scope: policy will be enforced at the request-router layer (policy table keyed by tenant id). It will select among existing model variants we host; it does not include automatic model migration or live hot-migration of model weights.
- Residency: we can guarantee inference execution in us-west-2 for pinned tenants by reserving capacity or tagging routing rules, but we need an operations plan for capacity reservation (Dedicated or private nodes) to meet their p95 needs during burst windows.
- Telemetry: we'll provide structured audit logs (request id, tenant id, model variant id, timestamp, region) and a weekly snapshot export for the last 90 days. For SOC-style requests they asked about retention and signing — we'd need to involve Security for KMS/HSM commitments.

Open questions for Engineering (Markus):
1) Do we have any blockers in the serving runtime for policy-based routing at the router hop?
2) Is it feasible to hit p95 latency targets using reserved capacity + autoscaling, or will we need a prioritized lane for the tenant?

Ben — if Product confirms the scope above, would Silverline accept: (A) routing + region pinning MVP with 90-day audit snapshot and post-signature runbook, vs (B) the more conservative approach of region-only residency with on-demand export/backups? Please capture which option is more likely to close.

I'll draft the commitment language once Markus confirms feasibility.

Laura Bennett
Sr. PM, Enterprise Features | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Quick engineering readout. TL;DR: feasible with implementation work and an ops reservation plan.

Details:
- Router policy: we already have a lightweight rule-evaluation path for A/B routing. Extending it to include tenant-pin + region constraint is ~3 engineer-weeks (one backend, one runtime, one QA) for a first pass + a week for operational automation (policy rollout tooling).
- Performance: p50/p95 targets look achievable if we provision dedicated capacity for Silverline's peak. If they expect burst concurrency spikes (per the traffic model), we should offer an on-call escalation path + overprovision buffer or a prioritized request queue (which adds complexity).
- Audit logs: we can emit structured logs and wire them into S3 exports; signing with customer-managed CMKs requires Security signoff and a brief integration with our KMS plugin (2–3 weeks for the integration and test certs).

Risks / mitigations:
- If we attempt a global auto-migration of models to satisfy residency automatically, that's a large effort. Avoid in MVP; require explicit variant pinning.
- Capacity cost: Dedicated reservation for worst-case peak will materially increase TCO; propose we bake a short-term premium into the quote or implement burst credits.

Estimate for MVP delivery window: 6–8 weeks from triage + prioritized sprint slot. We can compress to 4–5 weeks only if we reallocate an ongoing sprint's capacity and authorize fast-track QA.

I'll be happy to sync with Security and Ops. Please advise on tradeoff preference (fast MVP with routing policy + audit exports + CMK integration vs conservative region-only residency with later routing feature).

— Markus
Markus Klein | Eng Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Emily / Silverline team — looping you back in with product and eng ETA. Monica and I ran through options with Laura and Markus. High-level proposal for Silverline to review: 

Option A (recommended): Scoped routing + residency MVP (6–8 weeks)
- Tenant pin to model variant + explicit region (us-west-2) enforcement.
- Structured audit logs + weekly 90-day snapshot export.
- CMK integration for export signing (security-assisted, delivered in same window).
- Pricing: committed reserved capacity + 6% uplift to cover priority lane/overprovision buffer.

Option B (conservative): Region residency only (3–4 weeks)
- Guarantee execution in us-west-2 by reserving capacity; no tenant-pin routing abstraction initially.
- Ad-hoc exports and audit support post-close (manual for first 90 days).
- Pricing: reserved capacity with no uplift, SLA credits instead of priority lane.

Please let us know which option aligns with Silverline's procurement timeline. If you need the commitment language in the CSAM, we can provide draft wording for both options today and incorporate into the term sheet for signature.

Next steps proposed by Ben:
- Silverline indicates option A or B today (or a prioritized preference).
- If Option A, authorize a 6–8 week build window and approve the capacity uplift; we’ll set up a weekly engineering sync and Security onboarding call.

Emily — happy to hop on a 30-min call this afternoon if helpful.

Ben Carter | Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
